function.mechanism: Water-soluble betalain pigments (mainly betanin) absorb visible light and provide red-violet coloration in foods.
common_food_categories: foods generally under GMP where authorized

adi.basis: EFSA (2015) did not establish a numerical ADI; concluded no safety concern under refined current-use exposure estimates.

efsa.key_finding: Re-evaluation concluded no numerical ADI could be established for E162 and no safety concern for refined exposure scenario; 2016 extension assessment also found no safety concern for hard candy use.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (1987), with nitrate-specification caveat and GMP-based use.

concerns.summary: JECFA highlighted nitrate as a component of beet red and emphasized specification control, with particular caution for foods for infants and young children.
No IARC carcinogenic classification was identified for betanin/beetroot red in the current IARC list dataset.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation summary indicates no safety concern at refined current-use exposure.
EFSA extension-of-use assessment (hard candy) indicates no safety concern.
JECFA assigned ADI 'not specified' under GMP/specification conditions.
US 21 CFR 73.40 allows use under GMP with exemption from certification.

populations: infants and young children (nitrate-specification sensitivity context)
adi_exceedance.notes: A numeric ADI is not set by EFSA/JECFA for this additive; EFSA refined exposure summary indicates no safety concern despite high-end toddler estimates.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators (EFSA, FDA/eCFR, JECFA) allow use with no current strong safety signal, but EFSA did not set a numerical ADI and JECFA flagged nitrate-specification management, especially relevant to younger populations.
key_factors: EU and US regulatory allowance with defined conditions
Nitrate-specification caveat and limited modern additive-specific long-term human safety datasets
